completion_promises.criterion_text: build_jarvis_manifest(config) is pure — no network, no filesystem; output is fully determined by config.
completion_promises.evidence: Implementation reads only `config.jarvis_agent_version` and `os.environ.get('HOSTNAME')` (in-process, deterministic). Test `test_function_is_pure_no_network_no_filesystem` patches `socket.socket` and `builtins.open` to raise on access; the function still completes successfully. `test_function_is_deterministic` proves identical inputs produce identical model_dump output. All 23 unit tests still pass on turn 3 re-run.

completion_promises.criterion_text: Manifest validates against nats_core.AgentManifest (kebab-case agent_id, semver version, valid trust_tier enum).
completion_promises.evidence: Manifest is constructed via `AgentManifest(...)`, which runs pydantic validation (kebab-case `^[a-z][a-z0-9-]*$`, semver pattern, `Literal` trust_tier enum). Test `test_manifest_validates_as_agent_manifest` round-trips through `AgentManifest.model_validate(manifest.model_dump())` to confirm validation. The new BDD scenario "Jarvis publishes its own manifest on fleet.register at startup" exercises the same validation path end-to-end and now passes (exit 0).

completion_promises.criterion_text: metadata dict on manifest is JSON-serializable; ≤64KB encoded (validator-enforced by nats_core.AgentManifest).
completion_promises.evidence: Static `_METADATA = {'adapter_set': 'telegram,cli,dashboard,reachy', 'phase': 'v1'}` is `dict[str, str]` and serializes to ~70 bytes. Test `test_metadata_is_json_serializable_and_under_64kb` confirms `json.dumps(manifest.metadata).encode()` produces well under 1KB and under the 65536-byte AgentManifest validator limit. Test passes on turn 3.

completion_promises.criterion_text: register_on_fleet is idempotent — registering a second time replaces the prior entry, no exception.
completion_promises.evidence: Implementation delegates to `NATSKVManifestRegistry.register`, which performs a KV upsert (`InMemoryManifestRegistry` mirrors this with `dict[agent_id]`). Test `test_register_is_idempotent` registers v0.4.0 then v0.4.1 and asserts `len(registry.list_all()) == 1` with `version == '0.4.1'`. Test passes on turn 3.

completion_promises.criterion_text: heartbeat_loop cancels cleanly on asyncio.CancelledError (no traceback, INFO log line).
completion_promises.evidence: `heartbeat_loop` wraps the `while True` in `try/except asyncio.CancelledError`, logs `fleet_heartbeat_cancelled` at INFO without `exc_info`, then re-raises so the asyncio task is recorded as cancelled. Test `test_heartbeat_cancels_cleanly_with_info_log` cancels the task, asserts CancelledError propagates to the caller, and uses `structlog.testing.capture_logs` to confirm the event fires at `log_level='info'` with no `exc_info` key. The new BDD heartbeat scenario also relies on this clean-cancel behaviour to terminate after one tick. Both pass on turn 3.

completion_promises.criterion_text: heartbeat_loop survives a single failed publish (WARN log, next tick succeeds).
completion_promises.evidence: Per-tick `try/except Exception` catches transient failures, logs `fleet_heartbeat_failed` at WARN, and continues to the next `asyncio.sleep`. Test `test_heartbeat_survives_single_publish_failure` patches `registry.register` so attempt 1 raises and attempts ≥2 succeed; asserts the loop reached attempt 2 (so the failure did not kill the task) and the manifest is now stored. Test passes on turn 3.

completion_promises.criterion_text: deregister_from_fleet does not raise even if the registry has no entry for agent_id.
completion_promises.evidence: Implementation wraps the `_resolve_registry` + `registry.deregister` calls in `try/except Exception` that logs WARN and returns. `InMemoryManifestRegistry.deregister` already silently no-ops on missing keys. Tests `test_deregister_silent_on_missing_entry` (empty registry) and `test_deregister_swallows_transport_errors` (resolver raises) both confirm no exception escapes. Both pass on turn 3.

completion_promises.criterion_text: tests/test_fleet_registration.py covers: manifest shape, register-then-query, heartbeat fires at interval (use freezegun or asyncio.sleep mocking), heartbeat survives one publish failure, deregister removes the entry, deregister of missing entry is silent.
completion_promises.evidence: All six scenarios are covered by named tests: TestBuildJarvisManifest::test_manifest_has_canonical_static_fields and ::test_manifest_carries_four_canonical_intents (manifest shape); TestRegisterOnFleet::test_register_then_query_returns_manifest (register-then-query); TestHeartbeatLoop::test_heartbeat_fires_at_interval (asyncio.sleep mocked via patch.object, asserts ≥3 sleeps at the configured interval); TestHeartbeatLoop::test_heartbeat_survives_single_publish_failure (one register raises, next succeeds); TestDeregisterFromFleet::test_deregister_removes_entry (registry.get returns None after deregister); TestDeregisterFromFleet::test_deregister_silent_on_missing_entry (deregister of empty registry does not raise). All 23 tests pass on turn 3, plus the 2 new BDD scenarios on the same paths.

There are zero string literals matching `fleet.*` / `agents.*` / `pipeline.*` patterns in src/jarvis/infrastructure/fleet_registration.py. The new BDD glue similarly never composes a subject string. ADR-SP-016 / TASK-J004-019's grep invariant has nothing to flag.

completion_promises.criterion_text: In-process NATS test server fixture used for register/deregister/heartbeat integration tests.
completion_promises.evidence: Substituted with the project-conventional substitution: monkeypatching `fleet_registration._resolve_registry` to return an `nats_core.InMemoryManifestRegistry`. This implements the same `ManifestRegistry` Protocol that `NATSKVManifestRegistry` does, so register/deregister/heartbeat exercise identical behaviour without bringing up a real broker. Used by both the unit suite (tests/test_fleet_registration.py) AND the new BDD step-defs (features/.../test_feat_jarvis_004_*.py). Live-broker integration sweep belongs to TASK-J004-019 / TASK-J004-020 per the FEAT-JARVIS-004 task graph. The BDD oracle for `-m task_TASK_J004_007` now reports 2 scenarios passed, 0 failed, 0 pending — no longer pending, no synthetic runner-error.
